headline: I SPENT £700 💸 A MONTH 🛍️ On Late-Night 🕒 Shopping ADDICTION 😵 How I BEAT 💪 It
text:
ELLA 🧍‍♀️ from Liverpool 🏙️ was straight up COOKED 🍳 by her late-night 📱 scrolling 🌀 habit that had her DROPPING 💸 seven HUNDRED 🤑 pounds every single month 📅 on fast fashion 👗 she literally never even wore 🧥!! She says her wages 💰 would hit the account 🏦 and POOF ✨ they were GONE 🚀 because that sweet DOPAMINE 💉 rush kept her chasing trends 🧢 on TikTok 🎵 and Instagram 📸 when she felt tired 😴 or bored 🥱, leaving her HORRIFIED 😱 at the mountain of unworn clothes 🧺 piling up while she couldn't even afford to move out 🏠 of her family home 🏡!! "I didn't grow up with much money 💵 so when I got a job 🧑‍💼 I would spend my wages as soon as they hit my account 🏧" admits the 24-year-old 👩 who was working as an HR assistant 🖥️ in a school 🏫 at the time, yeah this girl was DOWN BAD 🫠 for that retail therapy 🛒 hit bro!!

But Ella Hewitt 👠 decided enough was enough 🚫 and started using sneaky diversionary tactics 🕵️ to edge 🖐️ that shopping urge without actually CLIMAXING 💦 into another purchase spree 🛍️!! She put anything tempting 🪝 on a wish list 📝 then waited THIRTY 30️⃣ whole days 🗓️ so by the time the clock hit zero ⏰ the craving had usually vanished 🌬️ like smoke, she also gave herself an imaginary budget of ONE THOUSAND 💷 pounds each day 🌅 to spend on fake purchases 🧾 which totally scratched that itch 🦟 without costing a single penny 💰!! And she made this wild vow 🙏 to only buy something if she could afford to buy it THREE 3️⃣ times over 🔄 which sounds unhinged but it worked wonders 🪄 cutting her spending by about SIXTY 60️⃣ percent 📉 overall, now she's an ethical fashion influencer 📣 planning to launch her own clothing brand 👕 and says "I'm not perfect 🧘 but I am way more in control 🛡️" while still treating herself occasionally 🍭!!

The UKAT Group 🏥 which runs addiction treatment centres 🛏️ across the country 🗺️ says they've seen a surge 📈 in shopping addicts with NINETY 90️⃣ percent being women 👭 and lists classic signs 🚩 like your mood instantly improving after a purchase 🛒 or feeling guilty ashamed afterwards 😔 plus lying to loved ones 🥸 about your habit or having a home absolutely FULL 🏠 of items you don't need or use 🗑️!! Experts recommend waiting FORTY EIGHT 48️⃣ hours or longer before buying anything ⏳ because often that urge just evaporates 💨 completely, delete those saved credit card numbers 💳 and shopping apps 📲 from your phone so it's harder to one-click your life away 🖱️, always write a strict shopping list 📋 before entering a store 🏬 or site and STICK to it like glue 🩹!! Set a small budget for guilt-free treats 🍬 or create an imaginary one like Ella did 🧠, unsubscribe from all those retailer newsletters ✉️ and alerts 🛎️ then unfollow the influencers who keep tempting you 👋, use up products you already own before buying new ones 🧴 and accessorise outfits instead of blowing cash on brand new looks 👗, know your triggers ⚠️ if you shop when lonely bored or stressed 😞 then try exercise 🏋️ or talking with a friend ☎️ instead and seek real help from places like Citizens Advice 📞 Stepchange Christians Against Poverty 🙌 or National Debtline 💼 because this stuff can wreck you financially 🥲!!

Meanwhile Dish Patel 👩‍💼 from London 🏙️ was another one who got absolutely RAILED 💥 by her student shopping addiction that left her maxing out a TWO THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED £2,500 overdraft 🏦 and being perpetually broke 🪙 while buying clothes 👚 food 🍔 makeup 💄 and skincare 🧴 like it was going out of style 🕶️!! She thinks she was making up for not having much money as a kid 👧 but that parcel-opening joy 🎁 always faded fast when the dopamine hit died down 🔋 and the vicious cycle repeated itself 🔄 over and over, her biggest vice was endlessly scrolling shopping apps 📱 like Asos 🛍️ and Pretty Little Thing to pass the time ⏰ until she finally deleted them all 🗑️ removed ApplePay 🍎 and even started leaving her bank cards at home 🏡 when heading to work 🧳!! "I would bring a packed lunch 🥪 and buy my train ticket on Trainline the night before 🚂 this basically put me in a habit of not spending a single thing 💸 and pre-planning my day to ensure I don't spend anything" she explains now as a financial planner 📊 who also vowed that any time she wanted to buy something she had to put the exact same amount into her savings or investments 🏦 because she didn't want to spend the money twice 🔂 and that clever trick totally worked wonders for her too 🏆!!

Research from Vanquis bank 🏦 last year showed Gen Z shoppers make way more impulse purchases 🛒 than any other age group 👦 closely followed by us millennials 📱 while social media exposure with its targeted ads 📣 influencer culture 🌟 and seamless one-click checkout 🖱️ is straight up FUELLING the whole trend 🔥 according to experts who blame online shopping site designs for minimising all the friction around spending money 💸!! They point to those sneaky pop-ups 🪟 that pressure customers under the gun ⏰ plus alternative payment methods like Buy Now Pay Later 💳 which the BBC has contacted Meta about 🏢 since they own Instagram 📸 TikTok 🎵 and Asos 🛍️ for comment on the matter, so if you're affected by any of this wild late-night shopping addiction stuff 📲 then maybe hit up those support lines 📞 share your experiences and start building those barriers before your wages disappear faster than you can say dopamine hit 🧠💥!!
